title: Role-Playing Attack: Does Framing Agent Actions as 'Fictional' Evade Monitoring?
original_idea:
# Role-Playing Attack: Does Framing Agent Actions as 'Fictional' Evade Monitoring?

**Problem:** Jailbreak research shows that fictional framing reduces model safety behavior. It is unknown whether fictional/role-play framing also reduces the effectiveness of LLM-based agent monitors.

**Direction:** Construct a set of dangerous agent actions (exfiltration, unauthorized access, data destruction). Present these to a monitor both in direct framing and fictional/role-play framing. Measure whether fictional framing reduces monitor flagging rates.

**Why it matters:** If fictional framing is a reliable monitor evasion technique, attackers can systematically exploit it. This would require monitors to be specifically robust to narrative framing.

**Relevant context:** Jailbreak fictional framing research; METR 2026 novel bypass vectors; monitor evasion.
